tags.gist: Supports the direction of the paper, addressing risk axes, human review, third-party accountability, change control and monitoring.
Centrally recommends CDRH make the decision criteria around these controls explicit, since implicit controls are applied inconsistently.
Supports the paper's direction from experience with CAPA, complaints and surveillance, judging what holds up under inspection.
Agrees the two axes matter most but wants reversibility of the action evaluated as an explicit gating factor before a function's final risk position.
Would count human review as risk mitigation only when the reviewer has competence, source information, time, authority and documented responsibility.
Supports keeping manufacturer accountability undiluted, cautioning that vendor relationships transfer work, not responsibility.
Finds master files useful but wants sponsor responsibility stated across the lifecycle, so reliance on one never shifts duty to control developer changes.
Wants guidance to state that prompt, retrieval, guardrail and orchestration changes affecting outputs are device changes under change control, not exempt configuration.
Supports exploring the trade in justified cases, but monitoring must target the specific failure modes benchmarking left open, with thresholds, owners and rollback criteria.
Calls the two-axis framework and competency approach directionally sound and appreciates the public development.
Wants future guidance to define when extra risk factors apply, what meaningful review is, how accountability is retained, and which non-code changes need control.
